https://mastodon.social/@schamspeare@mst.text: When I read that there are between six and eight new card sets a year, I just thought, how is this sustainable? But then I read that they also cycle as many older sets out. Okay, so it’s rigged both ways. The cards you bought are phased out, and there is a constant churn of new ones you have to buy to stay competitive. And with each new set, some new IP is introduced, watering down whatever was inherently Magic in Magic the Gathering. (7) #MTG #MTGArena #games

https://mastodon.social/@schamspeare@mst.name: schamspeare
https://mastodon.social/@schamspeare@mst.text: But that’s not most of us. Most of us find the obvious synergies, the ones that have been thought through and hardcoded into the game by the designers; or we copy what we see other players capitalizing on. If you’re in this latter group and you credit yourself with building a cool, powerful deck, that’s another illusion that you have fallen victim to. You’re one of tens of thousands who is reading the text and following the deck-building cues you’re given. (6) #MTG #MTGArena #games

https://mastodon.social/@schamspeare@mst.text: If you build a deck and win a few games with it, that’s probably as good as it gets. After that, you either keep playing with the same cards and at the same W / L rate, or you invest in packs of cards so that you can gain access to better cards. But the progress you make will be incremental and illusory when compared to the length of the climb and the essential balance of the game. (2) #MTG #MTGArena #games

https://mastodon.social/@schamspeare@mst.name: schamspeare
https://mastodon.social/@schamspeare@mst.text: Possibly final thoughts on #MTGArena after a week of casual play, no dollars spent: I don't really get what keeps people playing. Without a social element, you are in a rat race engineered to make you spend money. Even if you spend money, you will only inch forward and then hit another wall. There will always be someone with a better deck, you will never have all the cards, and the playing field will always be unequal. Unless you love a ladder, it will quickly become tedious. (1) #MTG #games
